control.name: Indexing program (absolute and incremental steps)
control.description: The control holds a program of steps; Cycle Start runs the next step. Each step turns the spindle to an angle (G90, absolute) or by an angle (G91, incremental), clockwise or counter-clockwise, and can repeat (loop count) before the next step.

citations.quote: Positioning of the workpiece is accomplished by “programming” the angular movements into the memory of the control and then pushing the Cycle Start switch on the front panel.
The control can be programmed to rotate the spindle in a clockwise or counter-clockwise direction with step sizes from .001 to 999.999°. There can be 99 different steps stored in memory.
You may store seven separate programs (Prog 0 - Prog 6).
G90 and G91 are used to select absolute (G90) or incremental (G91) motion.
The loop count display is three digits between 1 and 999 preceded by an L.
Resolution 0.001°

issues.message: Sources disagree on the maximum speed: 410 °/s on the Haas UK product page; the 2006 manual gives 330 °/s (specifications, PDF p. 4) and 320 °/s (features, PDF p. 3) for the brushless motor and 270 °/s for the brush motor. Used the product page: it describes the HA5C sold today and is where the photo comes from, while the 2006 manual may describe older units [INFERENCE].

The indexing program is described from the 2006 manual. This behaviour carries no program, so a build from these facts writes no program folder; the manual's examples run on a stored twin with python -m moonwalkers.control run (decision 0016). Whether today's HA5C control works the same way is not confirmed.

[INFERENCE] The drawing's dimensions were matched to views by where their text sits on the page (pypdf text positions): 15.32" and 8.3" sit by the Front View, 7.93" by the Top View. Daniel Sweet read 15.32" on the drawing as the full width, motor end to lever tip (2026-10-18), and 7.93" as the depth from the spindle nose to the back (2026-10-19). What 7.80" spans (printed right of the Side View, level with its spindle centreline) is not confirmed; no fact uses it.
